subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- November 15, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - November 15, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

We're excited to share the latest updates from the AcreetionOS project. Our team has been working hard to bring you the best possible experience, and we're proud to announce some significant developments.

Firstly, we're thrilled to introduce XRAID, a declustered parity RAID for zoned XFS. This new feature is designed to provide improved storage performance and reliability, making it a valuable addition to our distribution. You can learn more about XRAID in our community announcement.

In addition to XRAID, we've also issued security updates for various packages, including .NET, Firefox, and the kernel. These updates are now available for download and installation. We recommend updating your systems as soon as possible to ensure you have the latest security patches.

Rust 1.100.0 has been released, and we're excited to see the new features and improvements it brings. This release includes notable changes, such as the stabilization of the thread-local storage API. We're always looking for ways to improve our distribution, and Rust 1.100.0 is a great step forward.

We've also made some significant changes to our infrastructure, including the addition of new mirrors and a temporary mirror bootstrap process. These changes will help improve the stability and availability of our services.

In other news, our community has been busy working on various projects, including the AcreetionOS wiki and guides. We're grateful for the contributions and hard work of our community members.

We're also excited to announce that our newsletter is now available in an archive format, making it easier to access past issues. You can find the archive on our website.

As always, we're committed to providing a secure and private experience for our users. We're constantly working to improve our distribution and address any issues that may arise.

Thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. We're grateful for your support and look forward to continuing to work together to create a better Linux distribution.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift

Co-Lead Developers, AcreetionOS
